01 /Where we look next

Two paths. One open future.

From fundamental protocol questions to the frontier of open AI. Initial directions will evolve with researchers and domain experts.

01

Ethereum Strawmap
Research Track

Protocol & systems

Explore important questions in Ethereum protocol and systems research through independent validation, theoretical work, experiments, and reusable research tools.

  • Protocol and systems research questions
  • Independent review, validation, and extensions
  • Theoretical and empirical research; prototypes
  • Open tools for future research and engineering
02

Ethereum × Frontier
Open-Weight Models

Open AI & infrastructure

Investigate how Ethereum and frontier open-weight models can work together: sustainable economics, decentralized inference, verification, and shared infrastructure.

  • Economic sustainability and public infrastructure
  • Decentralized inference, verification, and incentives
  • Applications built on Ethereum rails
  • Contribution records, licensing, and maintenance
THE PURPOSE /A longer horizon

Good research needs
room to grow.

Some of the most important work takes time—and may not have an immediate commercial return. GCC is developing a long-term program to support independent researchers, small teams, and the people maintaining open infrastructure.

02 /More than funding

Resources for the work ahead.

Useful support looks different for every project. The program aims to connect the right people, knowledge, and resources.

↗

Research support

Potential funding for research and engineering, shaped around project goals, a work plan, and review feedback.

✳

People & perspective

Feedback from mentors and domain experts. Connections to universities, labs, maintainers, and open-source communities.

⌘

Tools to move forward

Help connecting compute, code review, testing, audits, technical discussions, and opportunities to share results.

Support type, amount, and duration depend on project review and available resources.

03 /Rooted locally. Connected globally.

A bridge from APAC
to the wider ecosystem.

GCC connects researchers, open-weight model teams, universities, and open-source communities across APAC and Chinese-speaking networks with global Ethereum research.

Universities & labsOpen-source communitiesResearchers & buildersResource partners

04 /From question to contribution

Start with a question
worth working on.

Independent researchers, engineers, small teams, and maintainers are welcome. Projects may come through direct proposals, referrals, or future research briefs and RFPs.

Submit a research proposal ↗
01

Describe the research

Share the question, why it matters, your approach, and the open outputs you plan to create.

02

Review the value

Review considers research value, ability to deliver, reusable outputs, and long-term impact. Track-specific criteria may be added.

03

Connect the support

Support decisions consider project needs, review feedback, available budget, and partner resources.

04

Build in the open

Create research, code, prototypes, data, or documentation that others can use. Sensitive findings may be released in stages.

Is the program only for researchers in APAC?

No. The program is open to researchers and teams worldwide. GCC’s APAC and Chinese-speaking networks provide an additional path into global Ethereum research.

For researchers, builders, and partners

What will you contribute?

Share your research question, work plan, and support needs through the application form.
